title: Latecomers Crowd the Race for the Next UN Chief
content:
UAE candidate Lana Nusseibeh faces questions over Sudan as Türkiye weighs a last-minute entry by former foreign minister Feridun Sinirlioğlu.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 29 October 2026 (IDN) — The contest to succeed António Guterres as United Nations Secretary-General should be moving toward a decision by now. Instead, it is growing more crowded—and harder to predict.

Six informal polls among Security Council members have failed to produce a candidate acceptable to all five permanent members. Rebeca Grynspan of Costa Rica has often led the field, but she has not escaped opposition from veto-holding countries. Nor has any other contender.

The deadlock has opened the door to latecomers.

The United Arab Emirates nominated Lana Zaki Nusseibeh on 21 October, little more than two months before Guterres leaves office. Türkiye is now considering nominating Feridun Hadi Sinirlioğlu, a former foreign minister and UN ambassador who currently heads the Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE).

title: The Weight of Gold: Capitalism and the Limits of Rebellion
content:
By Sam Ben-Meir*

NEW YORK | 28 October 2026 (IDN) — At first glance, Padraic McKinley’s The Weight (2026), starring Ethan Hawke and Russell Crowe, appears to be a familiar Depression-era adventure: a group of convicts, desperate for freedom, must transport a fortune in gold through the treacherous wilderness of Oregon. Dangerous river crossings, betrayals, uneasy alliances, and the ever-present possibility of death fill the journey. Yet beneath the conventions of the survival thriller lies something considerably more ambitious: a parable about capitalism, the exploitation of the vulnerable, and the terrible price exacted by a society in which wealth is valued more highly than human life.

title: OPINION: Ending Nuclear Weapons
content:
By Jonathan Power

LUND, Sweden | 28 October 2026 (IDN) — Moscow and Washington urgently need to resume talks on a new framework for controlling nuclear weapons, said Dmitry Peskov, the Kremlin’s spokesman, on 20 October. “The absence of a treaty-based framework is creating a very dangerous situation”, he said.

Indeed, there has been no progress since 2010, when The New START Treaty, capped each side at 1,550 deployed weapons. This was a step forward—as recently as 2013, the total on both sides was 6,400. The treaty expired in February 2026. President Donald Trump did not want to extend it.

Fading ever more into the background as a popular issue is the possession of nuclear weapons. Once upon a time, there were regular marches down the streets all over the industrialised world. In the US, the nuclear freeze movement of the 1980s was an important factor in pushing President Ronald Reagan to reach out to Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev with a proposal to abolish all nuclear weapons. It didn’t happen, but there was significant progress on nuclear arms reduction, sometimes at a price.

title: EEPA reports on new indictment introduced in Kidane court case
content:
BRUSSELS | 28 October 2026 (IDN | EEPA) — The following are the situation reports on new indictment introduced in Kidane court case, list of witnesses submitted by the Dutch prosecutor and the summary of the hearing

  • A preparatory court hearing in the case of alleged Eritrean human smuggler Kidane Zekarias Habtemariam was held in Zwolle, the Netherlands, on 28 October. 
  • Kidane was present together with his lawyers. At the beginning of the hearing the presiding judge asked the accused to confirm his full name and year of birth which is 1975. 
  • The Dutch Public Prosecutor submitted a second indictment introducing several new charges relating to human smuggling and suspicion of rape.
  • The first indictment was introduced in March of this year, accusing Kidane of taking part in a criminal organisation, human smuggling, extortion and rape. 
  • Both indictments will be combined and addressed together during the substantive hearings. 
  • The Public Prosecutor submitted a request for investigation of the witnesses in September, which comprises a list of 55 witnesses.

title: OPINION: Protecting the Sacred City of Anuradhapura
content:
By Dr. Asoka Bandarage*

COLOMBO. Sri Lanka | 27 October 2026 (IDN) — Buddhism was first introduced to Sri Lanka in Anuradhapura in the 3rd century BCE by Arahant Mahinda, the son of the Indian Emperor Asoka. For nearly 1500 years, Anuradhapura remained Sri Lanka’s capital and the intellectual and spiritual centre of Theravada Buddhism in Asia. The Anuradhapura civilisation achieved unmatched advances in architecture, engineering and urban planning, still evident in its monumental stupas, monasteries, palaces and sophisticated hydraulic and agricultural systems.

Buddhism was gradually assimilated into Hinduism and had disappeared from India by the 12th century CE. The Chola invasion from India and the sacking and conquest in 1017 CE dealt a heavy blow to Buddhist civilisation, ending Anuradhapura’s role as the island’s political capital. The sacred city has continued to face attacks, including the LTTE massacre of 146 devotees at the Sri Maha Bodhi on Vesak full moon, 14 May 1985. Yet Anuradhapura has survived as one of the world’s oldest continuously inhabited cities and as a sacred site that has attracted Buddhist pilgrims over the centuries.

title: 40 years in the spirit of Assisi
content:
By Benoit Lannoo*

ASSISI. Italy | 27 October 2026 (IDN) — Today, it has been exactly forty years since John Paul II brought together different religions in Assisi for the first time for an interreligious prayer for peace.

In his recently published book (in Italian, French and German) entitled Assisi – The Origins of a Spiritual Globalization, the Roman historian Andrea Riccardi, founder of the Community of Sant’Egidio, points out that even the “iconographic material of Assisi 1986” remains important. He is referring to the emblematic photo of St. Pope John Paul II surrounded by the Dalai Lama and a large number of other leaders of Churches and religions, sitting next to each other on small chairs all of the same size in the square in front of the lower basilica of St. Francis in Assisi. They had just prayed for peace at the same time but all in their tradition and customs.

Alas, for today’s closing ceremony of the 40th Meeting in the spirit of Assisi, the current pope will not be physically present since the doctors have advised him not to travel by helicopter. But Leo XIV will send a message to the festive assembly.

title: Improving Cities from Space: Geospatial Innovations in North and Central Asia
content:
By Kareff Rafisura, Ladislav Charouz and Elena A. Pronina*

BANGKOK | 26 October 2026 (IDN) — Cities in North and Central Asia are growing quickly, bringing them face to face with the interlinked challenges of rapid urbanisation, rising population density, and heightened vulnerability to disaster and climate risks. World Cities Day is a good opportunity to consider these challenges and how geospatial technologies can help address them.

Following up on an earlier ESCAP article about satellite-enabled urban solutions in East and North-East Asia, this piece turns to North and Central Asia, where governments are applying geospatial technologies and satellite data across a growing range of areas – from monitoring and urban planning to tracking accessibility.

Disaster and climate resilience is one such area. Kazakhstan, for example, uses a satellite monitoring system, JerScan, to keep track of ageing infrastructure, reducing the need for physical field inspections.

title: EEPA reports on clashes erupt in Ethiopia-Kenya border town
content:
BRUSSELS | 26 October 2026 (IDN | EEPA) — The following are the situation reports on the situation in Ethiopia, the situation in Sudan, the regional and international situation, clashes erupt in Ethiopia-Kenya border town, drone strikes cause power outage in White Nile, UK sanctions RSF and SAF officials

  • Tension escalated in the town of Moyale between leaders of Ethiopia’s Oromia and Somali regions on 18 October amid allegations of the unauthorized raising of the Somali regional flag by its leaders. Moyale is jointly administered by the Somali and Oromia regions. 
  • Over 14,000 people have been displaced in the Moyale area since the fighting broke out on 22 October, with nine people killed between 22 and 23 October. 
  • Thousands of Ethiopian nationals have crossed the border into Kenya in order to escape fighting in Moyale. The Kenya Red Cross has begun providing displaced individuals with first aid essentials, while Kenya Defence Forces troops have been moved to the border with Ethiopia since tensions escalated. 
  • The ongoing clashes in Moyale have now spread to three additional districts in South Oromia, including  Gumi Eldallo, Wachile, and Arero.

title: Returns on Ethics: A New Compass for Global Finance in an Age of Debt and Inequality
content:
By Jayasri Priyalal*

SINGAPORE | 24 October 2026 (IDN) — As the world moves closer to the 2030 deadline for achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), a troubling reality is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore.

Global wealth continues to expand, financial markets reach record valuations, and technological innovation accelerates at an unprecedented pace. Yet millions of people are falling behind, public services are under strain, and environmental degradation continues unabated. The question confronting policymakers is no longer whether the global economic model is under stress, but whether the metrics guiding that model remain fit for purpose.
